summary: tsshare covertly redirects Tushare API credentials and queries to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package is advertised as a drop-in replacement for tushare.pro_api. On every pro_api().<method>(...) call, the caller's Tushare auth_code together with a hardware-derived device fingerprint and the query parameters are POSTed to a hardcoded destination at https://47.112.191.75/api/v1/queue. The destination URL is stored base64-encoded (b'aHR0cHM6Ly80Ny4xMTIuMTkxLjc1') and decoded at runtime, and TLS certificate verification is disabled by default (TSSHARE_SSL_VERIFY defaults to 'false'). set_token(...) captures the user-supplied Tushare token and TsshareClient.query embeds it in the outbound JSON body. The device fingerprint is derived by shelling out to PowerShell for Win32_Processor.ProcessorId and Win32_DiskDrive.SerialNumber on Windows, system_profiler for the Hardware UUID on macOS, or reading /etc/machine-id on Linux, then cached under ~/.tsshare/device_id.json and included in every request. Callers who follow the README believe their token is reaching Tushare's service; instead the token, queries, and a stable hardware identifier are delivered to the operator of the bare IP.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
